title: Royal Canin Kitten vs Concept for Life Kitten
summary: Both are complete dry foods for kittens up to 12 months, sold at zooplus, and Concept for Life costs about 30% less per kilo at the nearest pack sizes.
evidence: zooplus.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, regular shop price without subscription or new-customer discount: Royal Canin Kitten 39.99 for 4 kg, Concept for Life Kitten 20.99 for 3 kg. Both pages call the food complete (Alleinfuttermittel). Analysis: Royal Canin 36% protein, 18% fat, 2.3% fibre. Concept for Life 38% protein, 20% fat, 2.5% fibre.
differences: The recipes differ. Royal Canin's page says 4th to 12th month. Concept for Life says up to 12 months and also covers pregnant and nursing cats. At the largest single bags the gap is smaller: Royal Canin 10 kg is 74.99 (7.50 per kg), Concept for Life 10 kg is 56.99 (5.70 per kg), about 24% less. We know of no feeding trial or test comparing these two.
why: The label shows a little more protein and fat in Concept for Life, for the same age of kitten, and it costs less per kilo in each size we checked.

title: Royal Canin Sterilised 37 vs Concept for Life Sterilised Cats

alternative.product: Concept for Life Sterilised Cats Lachs, 3 kg

summary: Both are complete dry foods for adult neutered cats with close protein and fat levels, and Concept for Life costs about 30% less per kilo at the nearest pack sizes.
evidence: zooplus.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, regular shop price without subscription: Royal Canin Sterilised 37 is 37.99 for 4 kg, Concept for Life Sterilised Cats Lachs is 19.99 for 3 kg. Both pages call the food complete for adult neutered cats. Analysis: Royal Canin 37% protein, 12% fat, about 6% fibre. Concept for Life 35% protein, 11% fat, 6% fibre.
differences: Royal Canin is poultry based. Concept for Life leads on salmon but also lists poultry protein and poultry fat, so it isn't poultry free even though the category name suggests it. Royal Canin has 2 points more protein. At 10 kg the gap narrows: 72.99 against 54.99, about 25% less. We know of no feeding trial or test comparing these two.
why: For an adult neutered cat the protein, fat and fibre on the two labels sit close together, and the Concept for Life bag costs less per kilo in each size we checked.

title: Royal Canin Mini Adult vs Concept for Life Mini Adult

alternative.product: Concept for Life Mini Adult, 4 kg

summary: Both are complete dry foods for adult small dogs up to 10 kg with almost the same protein and fat, and the same 4 kg bag costs a third less as Concept for Life.
evidence: zooplus.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, regular shop price: Royal Canin Mini Adult 27.49 for 4 kg, Concept for Life Mini Adult 18.49 for 4 kg. Both are labelled complete for adult dogs of small breeds from 10 months. Analysis: Royal Canin 27% protein, 16% fat, 1.7% fibre. Concept for Life 26% protein, 16% fat, 2% fibre.
differences: The first ingredients differ: wheat flour and dried poultry protein for Royal Canin, poultry protein and fresh chicken for Concept for Life. Royal Canin's 8 kg bag at 39.99 (5.00 per kg) is much better value than its 4 kg, so against Concept for Life's 2 x 4 kg at 32.99 (4.12 per kg) the saving falls to about 18%. We know of no feeding trial or test comparing these two.
why: Same dog size, same age, the same fat level and one point of protein apart, in the same bag size at the same shop. If you get through a lot, compare with Royal Canin's 8 kg bag first.

title: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB vs Intenso Premium Line 64 GB

brand.product: SanDisk Ultra USB-Stick, 64 GB, USB-A 3.2 Gen 1

key_ingredients.name: USB-A 3.2 Gen 1, read up to 130 MB/s, write up to 95 MB/s

alternative.product: Intenso Premium Line USB-Stick, 64 GB, USB-A 3.2 Gen 1

key_ingredients.name: USB-A 3.2 Gen 1, read and write speed not stated, metal case

summary: Both are 64 GB USB-A sticks on the 5 Gbit/s USB 3.2 Gen 1 standard, and Intenso costs about 24% less at alternate.
evidence: alternate.de product pages read on 6 to 7 November 2026, including VAT, both available immediately and with no crossed-out price: SanDisk Ultra 64 GB EUR 15.69, Intenso Premium Line 64 GB EUR 11.99. Both list USB-A 3.2 Gen 1 at 5 Gbit/s.
differences: SanDisk states read up to 130 MB/s and write up to 95 MB/s, and includes SanDisk SecureAccess encryption software. Alternate's page gives no speed for the Intenso, so it may be slower, especially at writing. Intenso has a metal body and is smaller, at 32 x 5 x 12 mm. Warranty isn't listed for either on these pages. Shipping starts at EUR 7.99, so this pays when added to a bigger order. No test we read covers these two.
why: For moving documents and photos now and then, the capacity and connection are the same. If you copy big files often, the SanDisk's stated speed may be worth the difference.
